Legend titles can be replaced with labs(fill = ...). plot() also maps the fixed-effect contribution with quantity = "fixed", several summaries at one scale are arranged in a grid, and side-by-side scales no longer carry panel titles.
  • plot() now respects limits for maps of signed quantities such as the spatial effect, which were previously rescaled, and arranges several summaries in two columns.
  • Maps of create_grid() grids outline the grid’s study boundary, so the edge of the study area is visible where the clipped cells end.
  • Several maps drawn in one call have wider side margins, so neighbouring legends no longer run into each other at narrow widths.
  • plot() accepts several quantities, for example quantity = c("fixed", "spatial"), and draws them side by side as it does for several summaries.
  • New assess_extrapolation() reports, for each prediction location, whether a prediction relies on extrapolation: covariates outside their observed range on the model’s scale, fixed-effect leverage relative to the data, and the share of the spatial variance not explained by the sampled locations. Locations are classed as supported, spatial, covariate, or spatial and covariate extrapolation, and plot() maps each indicator. Locations with missing covariates are drawn in grey without a legend key. The legend shows the colour of every class, including classes absent from the map, whose keys ggplot2 otherwise leaves blank.
  • create_grid() gains raster. The grid then consists of the cells of a projected SpatRaster with square cells: their centres are the grid points and the raster’s layers become columns, so values such as population counts aggregated to the grid’s resolution need no extraction. boundaries is optional in that case and, when given, selects cells according to keep.
  • New get_worldpop() downloads WorldPop population counts for a country and year, for the whole population or for chosen age groups and sexes, at 100 m or 1 km, from the unconstrained 2000-2020 or constrained 2015-2030 estimates, and returns one raster of people per cell.
  • to_table() is now generic and gains a method for predict() results with polygon summaries: one row per polygon, the mean and its interval in one column, probabilities as percentages and sums with thousands separators. All to_table() methods accept col_names. predict() output records the name of the weights column.
  • to_table() for predictions formats each sum on its own, so that values in a column are no longer padded to a common number of decimals.
  • Documentation and messages call phi the scale parameter of the spatial correlation function, rather than the spatial range, consistently with summary() and the MBG book. The practical range, where correlation falls to 0.05, is about 3 phi for the exponential correlation function.
  • predict() calculates its location summaries for all locations at once instead of one location at a time. The median and the interval limits come from a single partial sort of each location’s draws and are unchanged, and means and standard deviations agree with the previous values up to rounding in the last binary digit. On the 8,740 cells of tz_covariates, a predict() with the default summaries is about twice as fast, and one with every summary about three times as fast.

Cross validation

  • "user" has been added as an option to method the parameter of assess_prediction() replacing the previous behaviour where providing the user_split parameter overrode any provided method
  • In assess_prediction(), n_size has been renamed to size (for consistency with iter and fold) and which_metric has been renamed to metrics. Parameters have also been reordered: mandatory arguments first, then those required per method (in the order "cluster", "regularized", "user"), then the remaining optional arguments.
  • assess_prediction() takes a seed that makes the random splits generated for method = "cluster" or "regularized" reproducible, together with the refits and predictions of each test set.
  • assess_prediction()’s plot_fold = TRUE plots are now consistent across methods: "cluster" is unchanged (spatialsample::autoplot()), while "user" and "regularized" now plot the testing and training datasets.
  • assess_simulation() now takes fitted objects returned by glgpm() or model specifications returned by specify_glgpm() as its models templates. f_grid_target has been replaced by target, a function of the mean that defaults to the identity (see Simulations), and f_area_target has been renamed to area_summary. Their returned values are now checked before they are used. Grid- and area-level objectives can be requested together in one run with spatial_scale = c("grid", "area").
  • In plot_metric(); its which_score/which_model parameters have been renamed to metric/model.

Simulations

  • simulate_glgpm() now accepts a fitted model or specify_glgpm() model, with nsim, what, sample_locations, prediction_grid and seed. what = c("data", "surface") simulates jointly at the exact union of both sets of locations. This replaces simulate_surface() and its nearest-grid approximation. The old simulation arguments and output structure are removed. Parameters remain fixed, offsets and fitted inverse links are retained, and Poisson responses use exposure times the inverse-link mean. Use simulated_data(), simulated_surface() and simulated_values() to extract results.

  • assess_simulation() scores every model on the scale of the mean, each through its own inverse link. The truth is the simulated mean, which the generating model’s inverse link gives, and the predictive draws of each refitted model are mapped to the mean through that model’s inverse link. Generating models can therefore have any link, named or custom, and models whose links differ from the generating one, such as a probit model on simulations from a logit model, are scored on the same prevalence as the truth. A single function of the linear predictor was applied to every model before, which scored such a model through the wrong inverse link. The optional target is applied to the mean (the probability for a binomial model, the mean per unit exposure for a Poisson model and the value for a Gaussian model), so prevalence needs no argument, and other targets such as qlogis for the logit scale remain available.

Other

  • Argument checks in the compiled MALA, likelihood and distance kernels have been removed or moved to their R callers, following the contributing guide; the R functions already validated everything the MALA and likelihood kernels checked.
  • control_sim parameters have been renamed to control_mcmc.
  • to_table() now returns a directly renderable knitr_kable table, with an explicit digits argument that preserves trailing zeroes. This replaces the previous xtable return value. Values that are compared share one notation: when a value needs scientific notation, so do the estimate and limits of the same parameter, or the same metric for the other models.
  • summary() of a model with a nugget gave the wrong confidence interval for the nugget variance: its standard error was that of the logarithm of tau2 / sigma2^2 instead of tau2. The interval now uses the delta method for log(tau2) = log(tau2 / sigma2) + log(sigma2).
  • When one parameter has no standard error, as when a variance is estimated at zero, summary() and to_table() still give the confidence intervals of the other parameters. Previously all of them were missing.
  • The data_sf parameter in create_ids is now data.
  • The conf_level parameter in summary.RiskMap is now level
  • plot_metric() and plot_AnPIT() have been merged into a single plot.RiskMap_cross_validation() method. metric and model now default to every metric/model available rather than being required, so plot(cv_result) alone produces every plot the object has data for. metric accepts "PIT" as well as "CRPS"/"SCRPS"/"PIT_area" to select the calibration curve. Each metric gets its own plot (or, with more than one model, its own small grid with one panel per model); with more than one metric, each one is drawn in turn and the full set is returned invisibly as a named list.
  • plot_variogram() is now plot.RiskMap_variogram(), a method rather than a standalone function; call it as plot(variogram_result).
  • plot_sim_surf() is now plot.RiskMap_simulation(); call it as plot(sim_result, simulation = ...). It now draws a ggplot map matching the prediction maps, with palette and reverse_palette arguments. simulated_surface() returns an object of class RiskMap_simulated_surface with a matching plot() method.
  • In assess_prediction(), the "AnPIT" metric is now "PIT" and the AnPIT_area score is now PIT_area, for every family.
  • In plot.RiskMap_cross_validation(), the calibration-curve arguments mode, test_set and combine_panels are now pit_mode, pit_test_set and combine_pit.
  • Test coverage has been increased from 0 to 85 %.
